celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is, declare your Lord free of what is not befitting Him; «اسم» is redundant (zāʾid). ﴿الْأَعْلَى﴾: a ṣifa (adjective) of «ربك».

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى﴾ what He created: He made it proportioned in its parts, without disparity,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ﴾ what He willed ﴿فَهَدَى﴾ to what He decreed of good and evil,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعَى﴾: caused the herbage to grow,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ﴾, after the greenness, ﴿غُثَاءً﴾: dry, crumbled stubble, ﴿أَحْوَى﴾: black and withered.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ﴾ the Qur'an ﴿فَلَا تَنْسَى﴾ what you recite,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ that you forget, through the abrogation of its recitation and its ruling. He ﷺ used to recite aloud along with Jibrīl's recitation for fear of forgetting, so it is as if it were said to him: Do not hasten with it; you will not forget, so do not tire yourself by reciting it aloud. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ — He, Exalted is He — ﴿يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ﴾ of speech and action ﴿وَمَا يَخْفَى﴾ of both.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَى﴾: for the easy law, which is Islam.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾: admonish with the Qur'an ﴿إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَى﴾ — from the reminding of the one mentioned in «سيذكر» — meaning: and even if it does not benefit; it benefits some, and does not benefit some others.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿سَيَذَّكَّرُ﴾ by it ﴿مَنْ يَخْشَى﴾: fears Allah the Exalted, like the verse {فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ}.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا﴾, that is, the reminder, that is, he leaves it aside and pays no attention to it — ﴿الْأَشْقَى﴾, in the sense of «الشقي» ("the wretched one"), that is, the disbeliever,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿الَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرَى﴾: it is the Fire of the Hereafter, and the lesser one is the fire of this world.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا﴾ so as to find rest ﴿وَلَا يَحْيَى﴾ a pleasant life.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ﴾: has succeeded ﴿مَنْ تَزَكَّى﴾: purified himself through faith

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ﴾ saying "Allahu akbar" ﴿فَصَلَّى﴾ the five prayers. That is among the matters of the Hereafter, and the disbelievers of Mecca turn away from it.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ﴾ — with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] [تُؤْثِرُونَ] — ﴿الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ over the Hereafter,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾, that is, the success of the one who purifies himself and the Hereafter being better, ﴿لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى﴾, that is, those revealed before the Qur'an,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى﴾: these are ten scrolls for Ibrāhīm, and the Torah for Mūsā.
